al_turtle_rock_area_landslide_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulders filed in the Turtle Rock part of the Horse Pens 40 boulder field in St. Clair County, Alabama. Five problems are on record, running from a very easy slab through the middle grades and up to a four-star line at the top end of the range, so it suits a short visit rather than a full day. Expect the sloping holds that Horse Pens 40 is known for. The boulders sit among many neighbouring Turtle Rock sectors, which makes it easy to combine with other blocks nearby.

al_flintstone_the.blurb: The Flintstone is the final big formation in the line of rock that starts near the Sand Rock parking lot at Cherokee Rock Village, Cherokee County. From the lot you head right, passing the Holiday Block and The Islands. It is a compact spot with just five climbs on record: two boulder problems, two trad lines and one sport route. The roped climbs are around 5.10 and run roughly 50 to 60 feet, and a few of the older trad lines have been retro-bolted. The routes are on the valley-facing side of the formation, and the boulder problems range from V3 to V5.

al_lady_slipper_boulder_the.blurb: A single sandstone boulder in the Slider Boulders section of Horse Pens 40, near Steele in St. Clair County. It has five problems, mostly V2 with one V3, plus one very hard line at the top of the range that is far beyond the rest. The headline problem is a tall V2 that starts standing and ends in a mantle, which makes it a good one for mid-grade climbers. To find it, follow the wash trail from the Roadside Boulders past the Washout Boulders and the boulder is on your right. The surrounding Slider area is known for holds that reward crimping.

al_point_boulders_crown_boulder.blurb: One of several Point Boulders sectors at Horse Pens 40 in St. Clair County, Alabama. Five sandstone problems are filed here, three at V2 and two at V3, so it is a friendly stop for climbers in the low-to-middle grades. The most popular problem is a three-star V3 that has been logged far more often than anything else nearby. The spot is mostly shaded, picking up some sun late in the day, and sees light traffic. Walk toward the point and look for the last boulder on the left, next to the neighbouring Highlife boulder.

al_suspicion_boulders.blurb: A hard-leaning set of sandstone boulders at Horse Pens 40, near Steele in St. Clair County, Alabama. Five problems are on record, with one around V5, two at V6 and two at V8, so this is a destination for strong boulderers rather than a warm-up spot. The park as a whole is famous for sloping holds, and its best season runs through fall, winter and early spring when the friction is good. Several of the problems here carry two stars. It is one of many small sectors in the field, so it combines easily with others.

al_e_kill_taker.blurb: A small boulder in the Water Tower Area of the Hospital Boulders in Alabama, carrying a big face with striking crescent-shaped features. The namesake side faces downhill. It has five sandstone problems, from an easy one behind the boulder through V5 and V6 to two problems at V7, making it best for climbers who are already comfortable on technical slabs and slopers. Pads are advised, as there is rock in the landing. To get there from the neighbouring Shadow Lands boulder, continue to climber's right and a little downhill to the next boulder.

al_baby_fin.blurb: A shark-tooth shaped boulder at Middle Bishop, part of the Bishop Mountain bouldering area in Alabama. It is one of the first boulders you meet in the main cluster there. It has five sandstone problems, mostly easy to moderate: two at V1, then one each at V2, V3 and V4. Both a sit start and a stand start have good ratings, so beginners and mid-grade climbers can find something to do on one small block.
